definition: A superintelligence ban refers to proposed legal, ethical, or policy measures intended to restrict or prohibit the development of artificial superintelligence, AI systems that would surpass human cognitive abilities in nearly all domains.
details: The idea arises from concerns that such systems could become uncontrollable, potentially posing existential threats to humanity or causing severe social and economic disruption.

explainer.lead: Proposed legal, ethical or policy measures to restrict or prohibit development of artificial superintelligence, systems surpassing human cognition in nearly all domains. It matters because it frames the policy debate over uncontrollable systems and severe social and economic disruption.

tiers.eli5: A proposed rule saying nobody is allowed to build a computer brain far smarter than people, because it might be impossible to control.
tiers.practitioner: Policy and ethics researchers reference such bans when drafting governance proposals and thresholds; the pitfall is that capability thresholds are hard to define and verify, and broad prohibitions may be unenforceable or stifle beneficial work.
tiers.paperLevel: Defined as proposed legal, ethical or policy measures restricting or prohibiting development of artificial superintelligence; the concept is normative and does not specify operational criteria.

explainer.example: A jurisdiction drafting AI legislation could include a clause prohibiting development of systems that surpass human cognitive ability in nearly all domains.
